scope: Read-only self-contained instruction readiness review. Compared the exact R1 implementation instruction with accepted foundation public API and the R6/R8/R9/R13/R14/R15/R16/R17 contracts and the accepted Git kernel. No source, test, harness, build, Git, model, UI, network, or implementation action was performed. This report is the only requested review artifact written.

closed_checks.evidence: The instruction imports only resource_origin_plan, compile_code_proof_resources, CodeProofResourceError and CodeProofStructureError; it requires the plan resources tuple, retained exact eleven-byte dict and one compiler call. The accepted foundation exposes only CodeProofResourceError.reason and CodeProofStructureError.reason; the instruction correctly treats resource_origin/resource_hash/resource_shape and type/shape/limits as .reason values and forbids invented .type/.shape/.limits properties. It also keeps resource descriptors, bytes and compiled context session-owned through final verification and reverse cleanup.

The first paragraph requires exactly two Python fenced blocks followed by Tests not run and explicitly forbids file, shell, network and model tools, CLI/Git/source retrieval/Vault changes and existing-module changes. Runtime tests are confined to isolated temporary trees and genuine copied resources; no source or global os/fcntl mutation is authorized.

The eight fixed messages/codes, ValueError construction boundary, read-only copied properties, exact nine-field I/O shape, four-field limit shape, two-field conflict shape, closed enum values, 33-code prior-code union, bounded errno and final lineage/cleanup/original-exception precedence are explicit and consistent with R8/R9/R15/R16/R17. The instruction preserves unchanged CodeGitProofError/config/public/KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit objects when no higher-priority finalizer error overrides them.

The tests are told to copy the real eleven pinned resource bytes and preserve code_proof_resources.py in both genuine source and installed lexical layouts, patch only that module __file__ to select the genuine origin plan, and never override pins/compiler/registry or shared sources. This is executable at test runtime while remaining self-contained for the no-tool Builder response.

The exact builtin str .work/ grammar, controls/surrogates, NFC equality, named _MAX_BUNDLE_PATH_BYTES=16384, unattainable-positive note, no traversal before lexical checks, two-root complete-set capture, first-stage name/type/mode/link/size observations and zero body reads are concrete. Stable opposite-width/extra/missing reconciliation is also present, but its count/pointer ordering needs the bounded correction below.

R16 is incorporated: retain_input maximum is exact builtin int 65536 or 1048576 only, bool/subclasses rejected with CodeProofStructureError("limits") and suppressed context; fixed /input limit context is specified. The seven-key output setter has exact builtin dict/string keys/positive ints, copied values, one-call and install-before-set misuse messages, retrospective retained-data checks and hard maxima.

The retained graph, capability/lock/fsync ordering, no-follow descriptor seams, bounded scans, immutable first observations, installer phases, C+2*N accounting, same-temp-fd verification, no-replace link, checked cleanup, all reached final groups, reverse closes with duplicate lock last and no close retry, and explicit lineage > cleanup > original > success selection are concrete and consistent with R6/R8/R9/R13-R17.

findings.problem: The instruction says the initial raw root/object scan rejects hard count, per-body and aggregate caps before reading manifest, but does not bind the initial physical count pointer. Later it says raw physical object count uses /bodies, which is correct only for the post-manifest retained physical body-map check; R16 requires the pre-manifest raw count/aggregate admission pointer /objects. The body reconciliation list explicitly starts with width, then extra, then missing, while the accepted _validate_bodies_map first checks len(bodies) > max_objects, then width, then extra, then missing.
findings.impact: A Builder can emit the initial raw count refusal under /bodies, or check opposite-width/extra/missing before the max_objects cap. That changes the frozen instance pointer and refusal precedence and is not a deterministic implementation of the accepted kernel order.
findings.required_closure: Add one unambiguous stage sentence: before manifest/inventory exists, the initial physical raw-object count and raw aggregate admission use the hard max_objects/max_total_object_bytes contexts at /objects; after manifest/inventory validation, the retained physical body-map count uses /bodies with max_objects. Before any width/extra/missing reconciliation or body open, enforce count-cap first, then width, then extra, then missing. Preserve per-body and aggregate pointer rules exactly.
findings.required_tests: Assert initial over-count/aggregate refusals use /objects; post-manifest over-count uses /bodies; a post-manifest opposite-width-plus-extra input returns the count error when over count, otherwise invalid_oid_key before extra and missing; assert zero body opens for all stable reconciliation refusals.

findings.problem: The instruction closes retain_input maximum typing and error behavior, but only gives type annotations and prose for retain_input path and install relative_name/payload. It never states that path and relative_name must be exact builtin str and payload exact builtin bytes before Path construction, len/slicing, comparisons, hashing or descriptor traversal, nor does it assign a deterministic existing private error/context to malformed argument types, malformed install names or payload-shape/size refusal. R6 only says these APIs receive already validated internal primitive arguments and fail closed; that does not provide a self-contained runtime contract.
findings.impact: A Builder can accept str/bytes subclasses or path-like/adversarial objects and trigger arbitrary __fspath__, __str__, __bytes__, __len__, __hash__ or comparison behavior before refusal. It can also return arbitrary TypeError/ValueError or wrap private misuse in the public facade, making the private API and tests non-deterministic and potentially widening the fixed error surface.
findings.required_closure: Freeze exact builtin argument domains and first-failure taxonomy. At minimum require retain_input path and install relative_name to be exact builtin str, install payload to be exact builtin bytes, and reject before any conversion or inspection. Keep the already frozen retain_input maximum rule (exact builtin int 65536/1048576 -> CodeProofStructureError("limits"), suppressed). Explicitly choose the existing private CodeProofStructureError reason for wrong private argument shape (likely "type"), the fixed WORK_PATH_UNSAFE/path_spelling context for rejected lexical input/name, and the fixed limit context for valid payloads exceeding their selected cap; do not invent new codes or evaluate attacker-controlled formatting. State whether install misuse unwinds through the finalizer with the same private boundary.
findings.required_tests: Pass str/bytes subclasses, path-like objects, int/bool/subclass maxima, malformed relative names and oversized payloads with hostile __str__/__bytes__/__len__/__hash__/comparison methods. Assert no such hook is evaluated before the exact-type refusal and assert the exact existing class/code/reason/details for each case.

pointer_order_audit.initial_pre_manifest: Current instruction explicitly requires count/per-body/aggregate admission before manifest read but needs /objects for initial raw physical count; /objects is already explicit for aggregate and pre-inventory per-body contexts.
pointer_order_audit.post_manifest: Current instruction explicitly gives /bodies for post-manifest physical count and /objects for declared inventory/per-body/aggregate pointers, but needs the stage boundary sentence above.
pointer_order_audit.accepted_kernel_order: code_git_objects.py checks len(bodies)>max_objects, then every physical key width, then extras, then missing. The current instruction omits the first step from its numbered reconciliation order.
pointer_order_audit.decision: These are concrete readiness blockers, not implementation findings.

conclusion: R1 incorporates the five R17 closures and is otherwise self-contained, zero-egress, fixture-feasible and consistent with the accepted foundation and pure Git APIs. Dispatch should remain blocked until the two narrow clarifications above are incorporated and rehashed; no source or implementation action is authorized by this review.
